subject: A little help with data manipulation / reducing duplication please...

messages.author: 24877ba29ea4e175
messages.subject: A little help with data manipulation / reducing duplication please...
parts:
Dear ggplot2 discussion group

I am relatively new to R, but am sufficiently accomplished to realise
that I would like to use ggplot2 to produce a large number of
histograms. Please note, I realised this after dedicating an extremely
large amount of time and script to produce histograms using R: base
graphics. To avoid making the same mistake again I need your help...

I have a very simple data set of individual fish lengths (mm)
containing 3 columns (Site, Survey Year and Length). See the top ten
rows below:
Site Survey year Length
Deepcar 2000 190
Deepcar 2000 218
Deepcar 2000 270
Deepcar 2001 80
Deepcar 2001 192
Deepcar 2001 260
Deepcar 2001 245
Deepcar 2002 85
Deepcar 2002 90
Deepcar 2002 110


I would like to produce groups of length frequency histograms for all
survey years (10) at each site. However, I have 50 sites, i.e. I would
like to end up with 50 pages of histograms with 10 per page. I could
obviously subset the data to select each “site” and then write an
individual line of plot script for each site. However, I am absolutely
convinced this is not the most efficient or succinct method!
Therefore, I would greatly appreciate your advice on data manipulation
or methods to reduce script duplication, especially if the script
avoids referring to individual sites, i.e. only the column is referred
to.

Any help would be gratefully received!!!

Kind regards,

Jonathan

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: A little help with data manipulation / reducing duplication please...
parts:
Something like this perhaps (have not tested of course as we don't have your data):

plotfunc <- function(site) {
p <- ggplot(df[df$Site == site], aes(x = Length)) +
geom_histogram() +
facet_wrap(~ year)
ggsave(paste(site, ".jpeg", sep=""))
}

#make a list of site names
sitelist <- as.list(unique(df$Site))

# repeat function for each site, which should render a ggplot and save to your working directory
do.call(plotfunc, sitelist)
